title: Bound fixed-word centre gauges and exhibit the full-frame cost counterexample
body:
This package gives scoped negative results for frame gauges on one historical scalar word. It proves a total native-rank bound for all 511 fixed nonzero translation lines, stronger cost bounds for specified smaller families, and a sharp local rank-six bound for arbitrary common-line products. It also retains a counterexample to a broader cost claim. **It does not improve the complete kappa calculation or supply a new multiplication algorithm.**

Read the [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bf674b24f7ac83d67b9249ac2ad44efab14860a4/research/fixed-word-gauge-limits/PROOF.md), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bf674b24f7ac83d67b9249ac2ad44efab14860a4/research/fixed-word-gauge-limits/SOURCES.json), [decisive replay receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bf674b24f7ac83d67b9249ac2ad44efab14860a4/research/fixed-word-gauge-limits/evidence/replay/REPLAY.json), and [independent publication review](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bf674b24f7ac83d67b9249ac2ad44efab14860a4/research/publication-reviews/fixed-word-gauge-limits/REVIEW.md).

| Allowed gauge class | Result |
| --- | --- |
| One nonzero translation line fixed across the whole word; each scalar component chooses `I` or `C_a` | All 511 lines have minimum total native-rank change zero. Each even line is also nondecreasing on each native edge. The result does not settle all child moments for odd lines outside the common family. |
| One of the 16 common odd lines; the binary product `C_128 C_256`; or the four states `I,C_128,C_256,C_128 C_256` | Every increasing concave native-rank cost with `f(0)=0` is nondecreasing. Every zero-total-rank choice is constant on all 1,971 native components. |
| Binary `I,T_415` in forward coordinates | Minimum total-rank change is zero, but one cut removes a paid child and adds rank 48. Every changed native cut increases `sum r^(1-b)` by more than `47/9800` for `0 <= b <= 2/5`. The backward claim uses `F T_415 F^-1`. |
| Arbitrary products of translation lines from the common five-dimensional subspace, at both ends of a centre descent | Each descent has rank at least six, attained by `C_128 C_256` at all eight centres. This local theorem does not price the full graph. |

The graph keeps the scalar word and every native event position. Its endpoint condition is `diag(G_out) P = P diag(G_in)`. The proof charges all 5,064 native events, including 1,570 old rank-zero wrappers. It does not give a lower bound for arbitrary centre encodings, changed scalar schedules, or all Clifford gauges. The counterexample prevents extension of the concave-cost claim to the full-frame family.

The consumed source is the [pinned historical replay archive](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f/research/community-frontier1042-audit/selected-replay.tar.gz) at `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`. The package contains its two exact scalar-word and local-program members. The publication base is `b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51`; its [selected record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/b58ad9ef4d4e861b0eaa5dba41742bdc072dca51/certificates/selected-result.json) identifies [PR #4470](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4470). No transfer to that changed construction is proved. [PR #4700](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4700) gives a [different chart bound](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/34434d4ea5d9edf58529eaf79b543cd6c58f3e41/research/center-chart-bound/PROOF.md) on a different scalar word and allowed class. It is related work, not a consumed premise.

The [retained T16 notice](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bf674b24f7ac83d67b9249ac2ad44efab14860a4/research/fixed-word-gauge-limits/notices/research/gauge44-slots-t16/t16/NOTICE.md) credits @jeremykothe2 for the [PR #799](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/799) local word, @chafreaky for the [PR #741](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/741) frames and [PR #685](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/685) owner construction, and @FanPUYen for T16 integration. The [package notice](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bf674b24f7ac83d67b9249ac2ad44efab14860a4/research/fixed-word-gauge-limits/NOTICE.md) preserves the source gauge and pipeline credit to @icekylinx, the recurrence correction credit to @rohanarun, and the earlier supplier and controller credits and Apache-2.0 license. The source-domain lane supplied the certificates and product argument; temporal-reuse and encoded-controller supplied separate checks. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance was used. These are separate agent reviews, not independent human peer review.

Use Python 3.10 or later, the standard library, one process at a time, and at least 3 GiB of free space. From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/fixed-word-gauge-limits/replay.py --out /tmp/fixed-word-gauge-replay
```

The output directory must not exist. The expected final line is:

```text
PASS_FIXED_WORD_GAUGE_LIMITS
```

All nine checks passed in an independent relocated replay with a read-only package and an empty `PATH`. They checked both scalar endpoints on all 712 input columns, the complete graph, ranks by span and symplectic pairing methods, 10,488 integer paths, 3,384 common-line rank flow/cut cases, 800 common-line capped-cost cases, and 13 rejected damage controls. All nine mathematical receipts agree with the packaged evidence; five match byte for byte, and the rest differ only in paths or measured memory use. The review also checked the historical archive, source pins, checker adaptations, and the sharp local bound.

No current selected-construction cold replay, changed native circuit emission, full recursive repricing, hosting construction, or new mathematical search ran. The all-size compiler, physical supplier, precision, hosting, and analytic obligations remain outside this package. [Open next questions](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/bf674b24f7ac83d67b9249ac2ad44efab14860a4/research/fixed-word-gauge-limits/README.md#open-next-questions) state the remaining scope boundaries.
